description: The far end of the OCCURS 9 admin menu table and the third leg of gate G33: a re-entry carrying CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1, an AID of DFHENTER and OPTIONI '9 ', where 9 is the HIGHEST SUBSCRIPT the table declaration admits and is rejected all the same. app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy:45 declares CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT OCCURS 9 TIMES while :20 declares CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT PIC 9(02) VALUE 4, and both the guard at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:128 and the loop bound at :229 compare against the COUNT and never against the table's SIZE - so the nine and the four are two independent facts about one table, and this is the single input that makes their independence observable. case05 makes the last-ACTIVE-element assertion at subscript 4 and case06 approaches subscripts 5 to 9 from the unwritten side; this case takes the one subscript that is simultaneously the table's last slot and past the count, which is what tells 'the table has nine slots' apart from 'the menu offers nine options'. A translation that bounded the guard by the table size rather than by the active count - AdminMenuOptions.TABLE_SIZE instead of AdminMenuOptions.ACTIVE_OPTION_COUNT, the two constants being 9 and 4 - would admit 9 here, fall through to line 137 and index a slot that carries no value at all; the two-character OPTIONO echo and the eighty-byte message below are what report that.  Why '9 ' becomes '09' is the whole of lines 117 to 125, and every step of that chain does work on this input shape rather than being a no-op. (1) The descending scan at 117-121 starts at WS-IDX = LENGTH OF OPTIONI, and app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY:132 declares OPTIONI PIC X(2), so it starts at 2; byte 2 is a space so the first exit term fails, and 2 is not 1 so the second fails too - the loop varies and tests again at 1, where byte 1 is '9', which is NOT = SPACES, and it exits with WS-IDX = 1, never 0, because COBOL has no subscript 0. (2) Line 122 sends OPTIONI(1:1), one character, into WS-OPTION-X, declared PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT at line 45: the '9' lands in byte 2 and byte 1 is space-filled, so the field holds ' 9'. (3) Line 123's INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' turns that leading space into a zero, giving '09'. (4) Line 124 moves '09' into WS-OPTION PIC 9(02), which is 9. (5) Line 125 echoes WS-OPTION into OPTIONO. case10's '03' arrives already zero-padded, so its scan stops on its first test and its INSPECT has no space to replace, and case08's ' 1' is the mirror image with the digit in byte 2; this case and case12 are the unpadded form, digit first and space second.  The guard at 127 to 129 is a single OR of three terms evaluated in source order and this case pins the MIDDLE one: WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC is false because the normalised image is '09' and '09' holds digits, WS-OPTION > CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT is 9 > 4 and is true and decides the condition, and WS-OPTION = ZEROS is false because 9 is not zero. That ordering is behaviour and not style, so each term is pinned by its own case rather than by one case that merely reaches the shared error path (G30): case11 carries the third term, and case08 - handed a one-entry table whose active count is 1 and whose option is 1 - carries the ACCEPTED side of this same comparison, which is what shows the relation to be strictly greater-than and not greater-or-equal. Within the middle term the three cases are separated by what the distance above the count MEANS, not merely by its size: case12's 5 is count + 1, the tightest boundary; case14's 12 is a fully occupied two-byte field eight above the count; and 9 is exactly the OCCURS bound, the largest subscript that addresses a declared slot.  OPTIONO below is therefore '09' and not blank, and not the '9 ' that arrived, even though the option was rejected - because line 125 runs BEFORE the guard at line 127. The echo is unconditional: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY normalises, echoes, and only then tests. A translation that moved the echo inside the accepted branch would leave OPTIONO holding the re-supplied image here, and one that echoed the raw received bytes would leave '9 '; both are two-character differences the field-for-field comparison reports, which is precisely why the echo is pinned on a path that rejects.  Lines 130 to 133 move 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, move the thirty-seven-character literal 'Please enter a valid option number...' into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at line 38, which space-fills and so leaves exactly forty-three trailing spaces, and perform SEND-MENU-SCREEN - a PERFORM and not a transfer, so control comes back. The screen IS repainted: SEND-MENU-SCREEN at 172-184 performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO and then BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at 226-263, which recomposes the four active lines from scratch, each 39 characters of PIC 9(02) + '. ' + PIC X(35) into a 40-character field, the number keeping the leading zero its PIC 9(02) declaration stores and character 40 keeping the space line 231 put there. The message colour is the MAP DEFAULT: app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157 declares ERRMSG with COLOR=RED, and the one colour COADM01C ever moves is the DFHGREEN of line 148, on the coming-soon path this case does not reach - so there is no colour move on this path at all, and DFHRED appears zero times in the program's 268 lines. CSSETATY is not among the nine copybooks lines 50 to 61 copy - COCOM01Y, COADM02Y, COADM01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - so there is no asterisk marker to expect either. Expecting either would be inventing behaviour.  Control then returns to line 137, whose IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is false by line 130, so everything it guards is skipped - and on this input that skip is the whole point. CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME(9) is never referenced at 138 and never at 143, the XCTL at 142-145 never happens, CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is never zeroed at 141, DFHGREEN is never moved at 148, the coming-soon STRING at 149-153 never runs and the second send at 154 never happens; no successor is named and the transaction ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CA00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of lines 107 to 110. Subscript 9 is the worst subscript in the table to dereference. COADM02Y.cpy:22-42 gives VALUE clauses to four entries of PIC 9(02) + PIC X(35) + PIC X(08), which is 4 x 45 = 180 bytes, and :44-45 then redefines that storage with a nine-element table, so the overlay spans 9 x 45 = 405 bytes and subscript 9 occupies bytes 361 to 405 - entirely inside the 225 bytes that lie past everything the copybook values. The redefining item is larger than the item it redefines, which is a property of the source and is reproduced rather than corrected. Not one value below is taken from that span, and the arrangement is preserved exactly as found: the count is not raised to 9, the table is not extended to nine valued entries, and the five unreachable slots are not removed (practice B5, and the far-subscript half of G33). One thing about the translation is worth saying plainly here, because the obvious assumption is wrong: AdminMenuOptions.optionBySubscript delegates the 1-based-to-0-based shift and the range rejection to FixedWidthRecord.occursElementOffsetOneBased over 1..9, and 9 is INSIDE that range, so the bounds check would NOT have rejected it. What keeps the slot unread is the error flag at line 137 and nothing else, which is exactly why this case exists as well as case06's preservation case.  The eight unpainted lines are recorded rather than papered over, because two different facts could explain them and only one does. The REENTER path performs NO output reset: MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO at line 89 sits inside the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER of line 87 and is therefore ENTER-only, and with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arriving as 1 this run never executes it. OPTN005O to OPTN012O are the unpainted image below all the same, and for the other reason - not because line 89 cleared them, but because BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS iterates only to CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT, so lines 5 to 12 are never written at all; the EVALUATE at 238-261 would in any case have arms only for subscripts 1 to 10, with WHEN OTHER / CONTINUE for the rest. That image is also exactly what a client continuing this pseudo-conversation re-supplies for those eight fields, so 'not reset' and 'never written' are indistinguishable in the observable output - a stateless projection holds no previous COADM1AO to preserve (G37). The service reads OPTIONI and nothing else from the received map, which is why OPTIONI is the only received field declared above: pinning an echo of eight lines the unit never receives would assert behaviour it cannot produce and would fail the very comparison it is meant to prove. Gate G38 is usually phrased around the DFHRED-plus-asterisk highlight CSSETATY applies, and none of that applies to this program; for COADM01C it resolves to exercising both the ENTER and the REENTER path and expecting the map default red, and this case carries the REENTER half.  CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT stays 1 throughout - line 88's SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER belongs to the first-entry branch this path did not take, and the error path never zeroes it as line 141 does on the transfer path - so all sixteen communication-area fields are handed back exactly as they arrived and no nextProgram is named. The area is fully populated and seeded from the real fixtures rather than invented: card 0500024453765740 with customer 000000050 and account 00000000050 is the first row of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, the three names are that customer's row of custdata.txt, and the 'Y' is that account's status in acctdata.txt - so the whole 160-byte area is shown to round-trip unmutated, not merely the handful of fields a sparse area populates. Every width above and below comes from a PICTURE clause and from nowhere else: the screen fields from the xxxI items of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY, the communication area from app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy by way of NavigationContext's own constants (practice B11).  The unit is the service, constructed and called directly with no HTTP, no MockMvc and no JobLauncher in the path (G51), so the thirteen items below are precisely what AdminMenuService produces: the twelve menu lines and the echoed option. The invocation is declared in screenRequest and not in jobParameters, because ParityCase permits job parameters only for a BATCH_JOB - they model a JCL PARM, and COADM01C is an online program reached by CSD transaction CA00 rather than by EXEC PGM= - so an online invocation has exactly one place it may live. TRNNAMEO, PGMNAMEO, TITLE01O, TITLE02O, CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are absent by design, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO reads FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at line 204 and belongs to the controller if the service is to stay deterministic; the values that paragraph would produce under this clock are 'CA00', 'COADM01C', the two CCDA titles of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy lines 19 and 22 - line 21's alternative title is commented out and line 22 is the live one - '07/19/22' and '23:12:32'. ERRMSGO is absent because the eighty-to-seventy-eight narrowing of line 177 is the controller's step, which case11 and case15 pin between them. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant COADM01C's own version footer at line 267 carries, so one clock governs every case in this directory and no two cases can differ by their clock (practice B7); US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default (practice B8).  One note for a reader comparing revisions. An earlier revision of this case ran the first-entry paint with a second administrator signed on - a subject case05 already covers, and a security file case16 already seeds with five administrator rows - and it left the far end of the OCCURS table untested. The claim that motivated it, that COADM01C composes the same four lines whoever is looking, rests on the copybook rather than on any one case: app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy declares no authorisation column at all, where app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy gives each of its ten options an X(01) user-type column that filters what a signed-on user may see. This revision therefore signs the same ADMIN001 on as case11 and case12, and differs from case12 in exactly three values - the case identifier, the received OPTIONI and the echoed OPTIONO - so that the one thing the pair isolates is the subscript.  Every expected value above is statically derived: read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY, the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms and the real fixtures in app/data/ASCII. There is no COBOL execution baseline behind it: none was produced, and none could be produced in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, a subprogram linkage rejected when an executable is requested, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from this repository altogether. Only the provenance of the expected values changes; the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field comparison rather than whole-string comparison, and the diff-count-of-zero gate per module all stand unchanged. Because provenance is a stated success criterion, the deviation is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than quietly absorbed - risk R-A, as ParityHarness's class documentation states it. No user-specified rule governs this fixture either: review_rules returns 'No user rules provided', and that absence lowers nothing - the enterprise substitutes cited above stand in place of project rules, B5 for preserving the unreachable slots exactly as found, B7 for the one pinned clock, B8 for naming the code page and the AID explicitly, and B11 for taking every width from a PICTURE clause.
